| item | reading |
|:--|:--|
| the change | `MultiSelectField` shows the author's `placeholder` (read off the field carrier, as the single-value branch reads it) as one muted plain-text span, first in the editable chip container, while the value is empty. It hides after a pick and returns when the value is emptied. `null` counts as empty, and `''` as no placeholder. The span carries no name, id or role. The container keeps its host `aria-labelledby` (PR objectui#11139), so the group's accessible name is unchanged. Readonly-empty keeps `EmptyValue`, and no-options keeps `OptionsEmptyState` |
| the control | A field with no `placeholder` renders the unchanged chip row, with no stock `common.selectOption` fallback. The review (① 5) judged that within the triage: the chip row already shows every option, and a stock fallback would change every existing multi-value field on every host |
| tests | Widget and catalog pins: `multi-select.json` shows "Select tags..." when empty and not after a pick, plus the controls. The ablation turns exactly the 5 placeholder-present cases red |

**Out of scope, one line:** on the object-bound form path, a form view's per-field `placeholder` override is written onto the FormField, while every widget reads the object field carrier. The forwarded `placeholder` prop is also dropped by `toDomProps`. So a view-level override reaches no widget that reads `field.placeholder` (single select, this widget, the inputs). The review judged it real by reading and pre-existing, the same declared-but-dropped class one layer up. **Acceptance notes, carrier: none; not filed.** Its reach was never measured at a public door (a form view whose section entry sets `placeholder` over an object field, rendered through `ObjectForm`), and that measurement is recorded on the seat post as the next step.
